question: Which of the following architectural techniques has been used primarily to decorate the Taj Mahal?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Pietra dura**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Pietra dura** is an inlay technique of using cut and fitted, highly polished colored stones to create images.
 
• This technique was widely used in the decoration of the **Taj Mahal** in Agra, India.
 
• The stones used in Pietra dura are typically hard and of high quality such as **lapis lazuli, agate, jasper, and jade**.
 
• The intricate floral and geometric designs in the Taj Mahal are a testament to the skilled craftsmanship involved in Pietra dura work.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tesserae**

 
 
• Tesserae are small blocks of stone, tile, glass, or other materials used in the creation of mosaics.
 
• They are typically cubic in shape and are used to create intricate designs and patterns.
 
• This technique is more commonly seen in ancient Roman and Byzantine mosaics.
 
 
 
• **Mosaic**
 
 
• A mosaic is a piece of art or image made from the assembling of small pieces of colored glass, stone, or other materials.
 
• Mosaics are often used as floor and wall decoration and were particularly popular in the Roman Empire.
 
 
 
• **Relief**
 
 
• Relief is a sculptural technique where the sculpted elements remain attached to a solid background of the same material.
 
• The term relief is from the Latin verb "relevo," meaning to raise.
 
• Reliefs are categorized by their degree of projection from the background: high relief, low relief (bas-relief), and sunken relief.
